Child labour is work that harms children or keeps them from school, and hazardous work is its most
dangerous form. This notebook uses UNICEF's latest estimates for countries and regions, and the
ILO's survey-by-survey estimates (ILOSTAT) of children in economic activity, child labour and
hazardous work, by age, sex, area, school attendance and economic sector. Read the module
[README](../README.md) and [data dictionary](../data_dictionary.md) first.

**How to use this notebook**

- Run each code chunk in order (the green arrow in RStudio, or Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Enter).
- Answer the questions under each **Your answer** heading.
- When you are done, click **Knit** to produce an HTML report to submit.

# Part 0. Load the data

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)

base <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eddiekasner/occupational-safety-health-datasets/main/modules/intl-unicef-ilo-child-labour/data"
read_module <- function(folder, name, ...) {
  local <- file.path("..", "data", folder, name)
  read_csv(if (file.exists(local)) local else file.path(base, folder, name), show_col_types = FALSE,
           ...)
}

# UNICEF: latest estimates for countries and regions
unicef <- read_module("tidy", "unicef_latest.csv")
# ILOSTAT: shares of children (%) and numbers of children (thousands), survey by survey
rates <- read_module("tidy", "rates.csv.gz")
counts <- read_module("tidy", "counts.csv.gz")

# The latest survey for each country, measure and breakdown in ILOSTAT
latest <- rates |>
  group_by(measure, iso3, breakdown) |>
  filter(year == max(year)) |>
  ungroup()
```

**Economic activity** includes all work by children; **child labour** is the part not allowed for
the child's age; **hazardous work** is the part that endangers health and safety. Values are
percentages of children in the group.

# Part 1. The global picture

```{r regions}
unicef |>
  filter(is_region, indicator == "Child labour (economic activities)", sex == "Total",
         grepl("UNICEF Rep.Regions|SDG regions - Global", area)) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, fct_reorder(area, value))) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Children aged 5 to 17 in child labour, 2020 to 2024",
       x = "Percentage of children", y = NULL)

unicef |>
  filter(!is_region, indicator == "Child labour (economic activities)", sex == "Total",
         age == "5-17") |>
  slice_max(value, n = 12) |>
  select(area, year, value, data_source)
```

**Questions**

1. About what share of the world's children are in child labour? Which region has the highest
   share, and how many times the global average is it?
2. Which countries have the highest shares? In what year was each estimate made, and why does
   that matter when you compare countries?

# Part 2. Age and sex

```{r age-sex}
latest |>
  filter(breakdown == "None", sex != "Total",
         measure %in% c("Economic activity", "Child labour", "Hazardous work")) |>
  group_by(measure, age, sex) |>
  summarise(median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE), countries = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(age, median, fill = sex)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~ measure) +
  labs(title = "Median share of children across countries (latest survey)",
       x = "Age", y = "Percentage of children", fill = NULL)
```

**Questions**

1. How do economic activity, child labour and hazardous work change with age? Why is child labour
   lower than economic activity for 15 to 17 year olds?
2. Boys are more often in child labour and hazardous work than girls. What kind of work might girls
   do that these measures miss? (Hint: look at the measures that include household chores.)
3. Why are fewer countries available for ages 5 to 11 than for ages 15 to 17?

**Your answer:**



# Part 3. Rural and urban, in and out of school

```{r area-school}
latest |>
  filter(breakdown != "None", sex == "Total", age == "5-17",
         measure %in% c("Child labour", "Hazardous work")) |>
  group_by(measure, breakdown, category) |>
  summarise(median = round(median(value, na.rm = TRUE), 1), countries = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

**Questions**

1. How much more common is child labour among rural children than urban children, and among
   children not attending school than those attending?
2. Does child labour keep children out of school, or does being out of school lead to child
   labour? What kind of data would you need to tell the two apart?

**Your answer:**



# Part 4. Where children work

```{r sectors}
counts |>
  filter(breakdown == "Economic sector", sex == "Total", age == "5-17",
         measure %in% c("Child labour", "Hazardous work"), category != "Total") |>
  group_by(measure, iso3) |>
  filter(year == max(year)) |>
  mutate(share = thousands / sum(thousands)) |>
  group_by(measure, category) |>
  summarise(median_share = round(median(share), 2), countries = n(), .groups = "drop")

counts |>
  filter(breakdown == "Status in employment", sex == "Total", age == "5-17",
         measure == "Child labour", category != "Total") |>
  group_by(iso3) |>
  filter(year == max(year)) |>
  mutate(share = thousands / sum(thousands)) |>
  group_by(category) |>
  summarise(median_share = round(median(share), 2), countries = n())
```

**Questions**

1. In which economic sector is child labour most common? Name three hazards children face in that
   sector.
2. Contributing family workers are the largest group of children in child labour: they work,
   unpaid, in a family farm or business. Why is this kind of work hard for labour inspectors to reach?

**Your answer:**



# Part 5. Hazardous work as an occupational hazard

```{r hazardous}
latest |>
  filter(breakdown == "None", sex == "Total", age == "15-17",
         measure %in% c("Economic activity", "Hazardous work")) |>
  select(measure, country, year, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = value, values_fn = max) |>
  mutate(share_of_working_children_in_hazardous_work = round(`Hazardous work` / `Economic activity`, 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(`Hazardous work`)) |>
  head(15)
```

**Questions**

1. Among 15 to 17 year olds who work, what share are in hazardous work in the countries with the
   most hazardous work? What does that suggest about the jobs available to adolescents?
2. Adolescents aged 15 to 17 may work legally in many countries, but not in hazardous work. List
   the hierarchy of controls for a hazard that working adolescents face (for example, pesticides
   or heavy loads in agriculture), and say which controls are realistic on a family farm.

**Your answer:**



# Part 6. Two agencies, one survey (ENVH 460/560)

```{r agencies}
unicef |>
  filter(!is_region, indicator == "Child labour (economic activities)", age == "5-17",
         sex == "Total") |>
  inner_join(rates |> filter(measure == "SDG 8.7.1: economic activity", age == "5-17",
                             breakdown == "None", sex == "Total"),
             by = c("area_code" = "iso3", "year"), suffix = c("_unicef", "_ilo")) |>
  mutate(survey_type = sub(" - .*", "", survey),
         difference = round(value_unicef - value_ilo, 1)) |>
  group_by(area, year, survey_type) |>
  slice_min(abs(difference), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(area, year, survey_type, value_unicef, value_ilo, difference) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(difference)))
```

**Questions**

1. For which types of survey do UNICEF and the ILO agree, and for which do they disagree? How large
   are the largest differences?
2. Both agencies say they measure the same SDG indicator from the same survey. Suggest reasons why
   their numbers could differ (think about questions on hours, hazards and household chores, and
   about which children are included).
3. If a ministry wants to report progress on SDG 8.7, which figure should it use? What should it
   say about the choice?

**Your answer:**



# Part 7. Trends within countries (ENVH 460/560)

```{r trends}
rates |>
  filter(measure == "Child labour", breakdown == "None", sex == "Total", age == "5-17",
         country %in% c("Colombia", "Ecuador", "El Salvador", "Zambia")) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, value, colour = survey)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(shape = !is.na(flag))) +
  facet_wrap(~ country, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Children aged 5 to 17 in child labour", x = NULL, y = "Percentage of children",
       colour = NULL, shape = "Flagged") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

**Questions**

1. In which of these countries did child labour fall, and in which did it rise?
2. Why should you compare only surveys of the same kind within a country? What do the flags tell
   you?
3. The SDG target was to end child labour by 2025. Using these countries, how far off was the
   world from that target?

**Your answer:**
